clips.title: What is BM25 and How Does it Work?
clips.why: A short, plain walk through BM25: its parts, the formula and a worked example, which is exactly the ranking inside kb search.
look: The key components: how often a word appears, how rare it is across documents, and the document's length.
In the worked example, which word moves the score most, and why.
clips.after: Our search.py is the same formula in about fifteen lines, with K1 = 1.2 and B = 0.75.

clips.title: The unreasonable effectiveness of BM25 for agentic search — Jo Kristian Bergum, Hornet.dev
clips.why: Jo Kristian Bergum argues that BM25 itself did not change; the user did. When the searcher is an agent, an old formula becomes a strong tool again.
look: What is different about an agent as a search user compared with a person typing two words.
Why that makes a simple, predictable ranking a good fit.
clips.after: Nova is that kind of user: if the first kb search misses, it can search again with better words.

clips.title: The unreasonable effectiveness of BM25 for agentic search — Jo Kristian Bergum, Hornet.dev
clips.why: How a model writes its search queries, which tells you why a keyword ranking still works for it.
look: What kind of queries a model writes when it has a search tool.
How that connects to rare, specific words like "proto" or "QA lock".
clips.after: That is also why the kb skill says to add --path when Nova is about to change a file: it gives the search a signal the words alone may miss.

clips.title: Grep or Embeddings? Agentic Search Over Company Documents — George He, LlamaIndex
clips.why: Why Claude Code itself searches code with plain text tools instead of a vector database, from a talk about agent search over company documents.
look: The reasons given for skipping embeddings in Claude Code.
Which of those reasons also hold for a small set of owned brain pages.
clips.after: The brain makes the same choice: 35 to a few hundred short pages, ranked by BM25, with no vector database to run.

practice.q: Finish the citation kb search prints for the CI page at commit 3fa91c2.
practice.why: path@sha pins the exact version, so a reviewer can open it with git show 3fa91c2:engineering/ci-map.md.

practice.q: Why not paste every brain page into Nova's prompt instead of searching?

options.text: Claude cannot read markdown in a prompt
options.why: It can. The problem is cost and focus.

options.text: Every run would pay for every page, most of them unrelated, and the pile grows every week
options.why: Search fetches the one or two pages a run needs, with a citation, at the moment it needs them.
They could be, but that does not fix paying for 35 pages on every turn.

practice.q: Put the steps of one kb search in order.
items: If the mirror is more than an hour old, run git pull --ff-only
Read the pages listed in index.json
Score every page with BM25 for the question
Boost pages whose applies_to matches --path, if given
Print the top 5 as rnd-kb/<path>@<sha> with title, effective confidence and reviewed date
practice.why: Fresh mirror first, then rank, then cite: the sha printed at the end is the commit the ranking read.

practice.q: Why is search.py written with only Python's standard library?

options.text: So the CLI, Nova's kb_search, the brain's test suite and the bot rank pages the same way, with nothing to install
options.why: One file, imported everywhere. If two readers ranked differently, the tests would measure a different search from the one Nova uses.
Speed is not the issue for a few hundred pages.

options.text: Because plugins may not contain dependencies
options.why: The choice is about agreement between readers, not a plugin rule.

practice.q: Page A is 2,000 words and says "proto" once. Page B is 120 words and says "proto" once. With BM25, which scores higher for "proto"?

options.text: A, because it has more text
options.why: Length is not a bonus. BM25 scores long pages down a little.

options.text: They are equal, one match each
options.why: The B setting adjusts each match for the page's length.

options.text: B, because a match in a short page counts for more
options.why: In a short page the word is a bigger part of what the page is about.
